selection_rationale: cand-gvr-effectiveness-02 (GVR vs LLM-only) is the strongest choice for CNSM: it directly tests an operationally-relevant mitigation architecture (generate–validate–repair) with a paired, falsifiable design, high venue relevance, manageable estimated calls, and reviewer support—while avoiding the higher dual-use/ethical exposure of adversarial-red-team experiments and the very large-factor cost/risk of cross-model transferability studies.
unresolved_uncertainties: Validator coverage blind spots and the extent to which GVR overfits to validator rules (residual unsafe modes may remain).
External validity: emulator fidelity versus production networks (how emulator-detected failures map to real-world harm).
Possibility that GVR introduces new, unvalidated failure modes or config churn not captured by the primary validator.
Operational cost and hosted-model availability risks impacting planned repair iterations and sample size.
Statistical dependence structure in paired tasks and appropriate handling for multiple comparisons and subgroup analyses.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Add validator-coverage diagnostics and include a secondary independent validator or randomized holdout checks to detect overfitting to validator rules.
Predefine and document detection/logging for newly introduced failure types and clear criteria for treating GVR as harmful (e.g., taxonomy + automated detectors).

Clarify and preregister full statistical analysis: exact McNemar implementation, handling of dependencies, multiple-comparison corrections, power/sample-size justification, and planned subgroup analyses.
Preregister repair-prompt templates, exact iteration-stopping rules (max 3), per-task model-call caps, and a runtime budget enforcement mechanism tied to cost/model-call limits.
Specify emulator fidelity targets and justify topology choices; document limits to external validity and a safe-publication/redaction policy for failure examples and traces.
